title: SSG selection spike (Astro/Eleventy/other): WCAG support, runner-embedding ease, build determinism — decide before M2
context: open-coding-curriculum is an open CC-BY (prose) / MIT (code) curriculum of beginner programming lessons with graded, runnable exercises across languages. Every exercise carries a reference solution proven correct in CI (solutionVerified:true), learner code runs zero-install in-browser via WASM, and all content is machine-readable structured data so third parties can build on it. The project targets absolute beginners — self-learners, public-library patrons, under-resourced school students, career-changers — and operates under a donated-compute lane with no server-side execution of learner code and no partner confirmed yet (verifiedNeed:false). The learner site (M2) must embed the in-browser WASM runner and meet WCAG-AA accessibility targets. The wrong SSG choice discovered at M2 build time would require a costly rewrite. The spike must conclude before M2 site work (occ-site-201) begins.
objective: Evaluate candidate SSGs (Astro, Eleventy, and any other viable option) against weighted criteria — WCAG-AA support, WASM runner embedding ease, build determinism, supply-chain footprint, maintenance burden — and record a binding SSG decision.
acceptanceCriteria: At least Astro and Eleventy are evaluated; additional candidates may be considered.
Evaluation criteria are applied and weighted: WCAG-AA support, ease of embedding the Pyodide WASM runner, build determinism/reproducibility, supply-chain footprint, and maintenance burden.
Each candidate is prototyped to the extent needed to validate the runner-embedding claim.
A binding SSG decision is recorded with rationale before any M2 site build task (occ-site-201) begins.
Spike report is reviewed by the Maintainer.
output: A spike report committed to the repository with SSG evaluation results, weighted scores, the binding SSG choice, and the rationale for that choice.
